name: McCORMACK, the Hon. Michael Francis

headline.note: Official biographies establish a private-media career at The Daily Advertiser and Riverina Media Group from 1981 to 2002, followed by McCormack's own media and publishing business from 2002 to 2010. Sources corroborate the sequence and private control but do not establish exact transition dates, hours, leave or the substantive full-time nature of the self-employed interval. Overlapping editor titles are not double-counted, and no private duration is inferred from year-only ranges.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and member biographies record commencement with a Daily Advertiser journalism cadetship in 1981 and promotion in 1988. Exact appointment date, employment basis, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employer control is supported, but year-only boundaries and missing full-time evidence prevent a duration.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and member biographies give the 1988–1991 title range. Exact promotion dates, hours, leave and any break are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: A title and year range do not independently establish a substantive full-time interval.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies record acting-editor service in 1991–1992. Exact dates, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: This title transition is retained separately without inventing calendar boundaries.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official records give 1992–2002; Charles Sturt University archives corroborate the editor years, and contemporaneous ABC reporting places suspension and departure in February 2002. Exact appointment and cessation days, hours and leave remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The private-media employer and broad continuity are established, but mixed-precision boundaries and missing full-time evidence prevent an exact duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies and McCormack's published history record the group-editor appointment from 1996 within the continuing Daily Advertiser editorship. Exact scope, transition date, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: This concurrent senior title must not be added to the underlying newspaper employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies give publisher service from 2002 to 2010; McCormack's own history says he started MSS in 2002. The election date bounds the endpoint but does not prove business cessation. Legal entity, exact dates, clients, hours, leave and continuity during campaign work are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may count only when substantive full-time work and boundaries are supported; ownership and title alone are insufficient.

career_spells.evidence_note: McCormack's published history and secondary synthesis record the 1994–2003 directorship. Remuneration, workload, exact dates and the historian arrangement are unresolved; the role overlapped newspaper employment and MSS.
career_spells.counting_note: Sporting-club governance is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.role: Chair, Kay Hull federal election campaign committees
career_spells.evidence_note: McCormack's published history identifies chairmanship of the 2004 and 2007 election campaign committees. It does not establish continuous service between elections, remuneration, hours or MSS overlap.
career_spells.counting_note: Party campaign organisation is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: McCormack's published history records this party office across 2010–2011, overlapping MSS and federal service. Remuneration, hours and exact dates are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official and member biographies establish House service from 21 August 2010. Ministerial, party-leadership and shadow-ministerial responsibilities are nested within elected office.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: The official newspaper chronology is preserved as sequential title spells; the group-editor role overlaps the Daily Advertiser editorship and is not double-counted.
The Daily Advertiser and Riverina Media Group are treated as private media employers at the time.
MSS is treated as private self-employment, but founding and publishing titles do not establish full-time work or exact continuity through the 2010 campaign.
Turf Club governance, party campaign roles, party office and federal elected office are separated and excluded under the codebook.
No private full-time total is calculated because exact boundaries, hours, leave and the substantive status of MSS remain unsupported.
open_questions: What were the exact appointment and promotion dates, contracted hours and leave across the Daily Advertiser and Riverina Media Group roles?
What was the employing legal entity and ownership structure of Riverina Media Group during each title phase?
What was the exact Daily Advertiser cessation date and the start date, legal entity, clients, remuneration, hours and leave for MSS?
Did MSS continue after the 21 August 2010 election or pause during preselection and campaigning?
Were the Murrumbidgee Turf Club director or historian roles remunerated, and what workload did they involve?
Were the 2004, 2007 and 2010 party/campaign roles remunerated, and how did they overlap MSS work?
